content: Swedish Bitters is a traditional herbal tonic that is believed to have been originally formulated by Paracelsus, a Swiss physician and alchemist, and later rediscovered by two 18th-century Swedish medical practitioners, Dr. Claus Samst and Dr. Urban Hjärne. In more recent times, it has been popularized by Maria Treben, an Austrian herbalist. This tonic is often claimed to have therapeutic properties, including the ability to treat a wide range of ailments and improve digestion. However, these claims are largely anecdotal and lack substantial scientific evidence to support them. One documented recipe for Swedish Bitters includes the following ingredients: aloe, myrrh, saffron, senna leaves, camphor, angelica root, zedoary root, manna, theriac venezian, carline thistle root, and rhubarb root. Variations of this recipe exist, and herbal shops offer both alcoholic and non-alcoholic versions of the tonic. The alcoholic version of Swedish Bitters is said to have a flavor profile similar to Angostura bitters, though it is described as being slightly drier in taste.
